messages.subject: Units of D.sum
parts:
I started a new thread for this query from Ujjwal

"One more question . What is the unit of D.sum(fx.total). say I have 25 hectare grid(500mX500m) spacing in mask file. is it per hectare or per grid(pixel, cell)???"

The help for fx.total says "All densities are in animals per hectare". If you take my advice and do not use fxi then you do not need to know this!

Murray

messages.subject: Re: Units of D.sum
parts:
Apologies for a naive question, but we need to export the density surface as a raster (TIF). Is there a way to multiply D.sum estimated using fx.total() with 10,000 to get density surface of the order of per 100 sq km? Currently low densities per hectare resulting in an exported raster file with no recognizable grid values. This is unless we are doing it wrong, and will appreciate any assistance..

Thanks, Koustubh.

messages.author: 118cea91a1619106
messages.subject: Re: Units of D.sum
parts:
D.sum is a covariate of the Dsurface object produced by fx.total, and I assume, perhaps wrongly, that you are using the raster function to export that as a RasterLayer. Although there is no 'scale' argument for the raster method (as there is for plot.Dsurface, you can generate a new covariate scaled appropriately and use that. I think something like this should work:
asurface <- fx.total(fittedmodel)
covariates(asurface)$Dsum10000 <- covariates(asurface)$Dsum * 10000
tmpraster <- raster(asurface, covariate = 'Dsum10000')
Murray
